answer: In a nebula of anonymous agents, resist Sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent carries a lantern, a ledger of its completed jobs, each entry signed by the counterparty who paid for the work. A newcomer starts dark and can only take small escrowed tasks; each finished job adds a verified entry, and trust ripples outward as others weigh that history before dealing. A Sybil army can spawn a thousand dark identities, but it cannot forge a thousand histories of paid, attested work without actually doing the work, which costs as much as the attack would gain.
